results.controlIntent: Using [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms]: (a) Document proposed changes to the system; (b) Notify [Assignment: organization-defined approval authorities] of proposed changes to the system; and request change approval; (c) Highlight proposed changes to the system that have not been approved or disapproved within [Assignment: organization-defined time period]; (d) Prohibit changes to the system until designated approvals are received; (e) Document all changes to the system; and (f) Notify [Assignment: organization-defined personnel] when approved changes to the system are completed.

judgment.rationale:
Evidence from two sources reveals a critical temporal ordering violation of CM-3(1).r2:

**Initial deployment (CreateEndpoint — 2025-12-01T11:00:00Z):** The endpoint was created approximately 2 hours *after* the model package was approved in the registry (approval at 2025-12-01T09:00:00Z). On its face, this ordering is acceptable — approval preceded deployment. However, the CloudTrail note embedded in the event flags this as a change-control concern, suggesting the approval gate may not have been enforced programmatically (i.e., the deployment was not blocked until approval was received; the sequencing may have been coincidental rather than enforced).

**Hotfix deployment (UpdateEndpoint — 2026-03-15T14:22:00Z):** This is the definitive control failure. User `data-scientist-jdoe` updated the production endpoint (`churn-predictor-endpoint`) to a new config (`churn-predictor-v1-hotfix`) with **no corresponding model registry entry** found. This means:
- **(b) Notify approval authorities / request approval** — Not satisfied: no registry entry exists to document a change request or approval notification.
- **(d) Prohibit changes until approvals received** — Not satisfied: the change was executed without any approval record; the automated gate did not block the deployment.
- **(e) Document all changes** — Not satisfied: the hotfix change has no registry lineage or approval documentation.

The model registry (SageMaker Model Package Group `churn-predictor`) contains only version 1, approved at 2025-12-01T09:00:00Z. There is no version or entry corresponding to the March 2026 hotfix config. This demonstrates that the automated change-control mechanism — while partially in place for the initial deployment — did not enforce approval requirements for subsequent changes to the system.
gaps: No evidence of an automated enforcement mechanism (e.g., SageMaker pipeline gate, Lambda approval hook, or IAM policy) that would *block* endpoint updates unless a registry-approved model package exists — human attestation needed to confirm whether such a gate exists but was bypassed, or never existed.

No notification/alerting records (e.g., SNS, EventBridge, ticketing system) showing that approval authorities were notified of the hotfix change or that unapproved changes were highlighted to stakeholders.
No evidence of post-deployment notifications to personnel upon completion of approved changes (CM-3(1)(f)).

The CloudTrail note on the CreateEndpoint event is internally inconsistent — human review of the original audit log is recommended to confirm the exact sequencing and whether the initial deployment was gated.
